record.original_question: In the discretized affine phase-retrieval formulation derived from the sparse crystallographic model, how many probe shifts are needed to guarantee unique recovery of the unknown feature weights a_j and locations t_j from the resulting phaseless measurements?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. How large the set of the probe shifts R should be to ensure unique reconstruction of aj , tj , j P {1, . . . , N} from (10)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $n \geq 1$ and $N \geq 1$. Consider a one-dimensional discrete object on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ of the sparse "crystallographic" form
$$\mathbf{f} = \mathbf{1} + \sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j\, \mathbf{e}_{t_j},$$
where $\mathbf{1}$ is the constant vector with all entries equal to $1$, the locations $t_1,\dots,t_N \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ are distinct, the weights $a_1,\dots,a_N \in \mathbb{C}$ are of the form $a_j = e^{i\omega_j}-1$ with $\omega_j \in \mathbb{R}$, and $\mathbf{e}_t$ denotes the standard basis vector concentrated at position $t$.

Let $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{C}^n$ be a fixed known probe vector, let $F$ denote the normalized discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^n$, and for $r \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ let $S_r$ denote the cyclic shift operator $(S_r \mathbf{w})_t = \mathbf{w}_{t-r}$. For a set of probe shifts $R \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, the phaseless measurements are
$$\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{f})(r,k) \;=\; \left| (F\mathbf{w})_k \;+\; \sum_{j=1}^{N} \frac{a_j}{\sqrt{n}}\, (S_r \mathbf{w})_{t_j}\, e^{-2\pi i k (t_j - r)/n} \right|^{2}, \qquad r \in R,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}.$$

Determine the minimum cardinality $|R|$ (and characterize the configurations of probe shifts $R$) that guarantees unique recovery of the unknown parameters $\{(a_j, t_j)\}_{j=1}^{N}$ from the measurements $\{\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{f})(r,k) : r \in R,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2026 survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval (arXiv:2505.15351), with no published resolution located in the related sparse / crystallographic phase retrieval literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing selected open problems in phase retrieval, including the question on the size of probe-shift sets for sparse crystallographic recovery.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an unresolved open question.

status_evidence.title: Toward a mathematical theory of the crystallographic phase retrieval problem
status_evidence.snippet: Studies uniqueness in crystallographic phase retrieval without addressing the specific probe-shift cardinality question for the affine model.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on crystallographic phase retrieval does not resolve this specific question.
